#9575. ProWritingAid VS Grammarly: Which Grammar Checker is Better in (2022) ?

Grammarly is a tool that checks for grammatical errors, spelling, and punctuation.it gives you comprehensive feedback on your writing. You can use this tool to proofread and edit articles, blog posts, emails, etc.

Grammarly also detects all types of mistakes, including sentence structure issues and misused words. It also gives you suggestions on style changes, punctuation, spelling, and grammar all are in real-time. The free version covers the basics like identifying grammar and spelling mistakes

whereas the Premium version offers a lot more functionality, it detects plagiarism in your content, suggests word choice, or adds fluency to it.

ProWritingAid is a style and grammar checker for content creators and writers. It helps to optimize word choice, punctuation errors, and common grammar mistakes, providing detailed reports to help you improve your writing.

ProWritingAid can be used as an add-on to WordPress, Gmail, and Google Docs. The software also offers helpful articles, videos, quizzes, and explanations to help improve your writing.

Here are some key features of ProWriting Aid:

Grammarly and ProWritingAid are well-known grammar-checking software. However, if you're like most people who can't decide which to use, here are some different points that may be helpful in your decision.

As both writing assistants are great in their own way, you need to choose the one that suits you best.

Both ProWritingAid and Grammarly are awesome writing tools, without a doubt. but as per my experience, Grammarly is a winner here because Grammarly helps you to review and edit your content. Grammarly highlights all the mistakes in your writing within seconds of copying and pasting the content into Grammarly’s editor or using the software’s native feature in other text editors.

Not only does it identify tiny grammatical and spelling errors, it tells you when you overlook punctuations where they are needed. And, beyond its plagiarism-checking capabilities, Grammarly helps you proofread your content. Even better, the software offers a free plan that gives you access to some of its features.

I use the paid versions of both Grammarly and Pro Writing Aid. Both of them have issues:- Grammarly IS more focused on nonfiction than fiction. If you're writing fiction, you may find Grammarly's insistence on "Conciseness" annoying. They seem to want to take the soul out of your writing, which is fine for a corporate report or technical manual, but not for your Great American Novel.- Grammarly pushes features on users that are not ready for prime time. It doesn't matter that you never agreed to be a beta tester for them; you get to do it anyway.- Pro Writing Aid actually counts the occurrences of words in your document and tells you when a word has been overused compared to published literature. Grammarly, on the other hand, seems hell-bent to remove certain words that it has deemed overused from the language, whether or not they're actually overused in your document.- Grammarly's Clarity function is simply horrible. It mangles sentences and changes their meaning. Sometimes the result of its suggestion is unintelligible garbage.- Grammarly allows you to turn off some checks, but not all of them. Unfortunately, the ones you cannot turn off are some of the most irritating (such as that horrible "Clarity"). On the other hand, Pro Writing Aid lets you choose which checks you use.- Pro Writing Aid has a mediocre command of American English (it's a British product). The app insists on rules of grammar and spelling that are outright wrong, per Merriam-Webster, the Chicago Manual of Style, and modern usage as shown by Google Books Ngram. At one point, Pro Writing Aid insisted that American English did not include the words "holiday" and "autumn," that "vacation" and "fall" must be used instead.- Pro Writing Aid's rules for commas are 100 percent consistent with the way I learned them in high school--50 years ago! They do not reflect modern usage. Grammarly is much better at this.- Pro Writing Aid seems to waste their limited resources on tweaking their UI. Their UI most definitely could use improvement, but these changes are not great improvements; they only serve to confuse users. Their resources would be better spent fixing the many functional problems in their app.- Some of Pro Writing Aid's checks are completely useless, as they do not take context into consideration. For example, an ordinary word would not be capitalized as part of a narrative, but would be as part of a title (for example, "professor." But if you capitalize correctly for context, Pro Writing Aid dings you for "Inconsistent capitalization." Similar issues exist with hyphenation consistency check.Each of these applications has its strengths as well as considerable weaknesses. I will say that both of them are light-years better than the execrable grammar checker in Microsoft Word, but that's damning with faint praise.

#9574. Quote and contract from the same numbers: a wedding vendor's spreadsheet + the 11 clauses that hold up

Every wedding vendor I have talked to has the same story. Somewhere around booking number twenty, a client cancels six weeks out, asks for the deposit back, and the vendor realises the "contract" was a WhatsApp message that said "ok booked!". The second-most-common story is the quote that got sent as a photo of a notes app, with one line item missing, and the argument that followed on the wedding day.

Both problems have the same fix: a quote and a contract that come from the same numbers. Here is the structure I use, with the spreadsheet logic that keeps the two in sync.

The mistake most vendors make is writing percentages in three places: the quote says "30% deposit", the contract says "40% second payment", and the payment reminder you send says something else. Put every rule in one place and let everything reference it:

The final-balance cell is a formula, not a number, so it can never fail to add up. A one-line check next to it (=IF(ROUND(dep+second+final,4)=1,"OK","CHECK")) catches the day you change the deposit and forget the rest.

A pricelist with a short code per item (PKG-03, ADD-06) means the quote sheet needs only two inputs per line: code and quantity. Name, unit and price come from a lookup:

INDEX/MATCH rather than XLOOKUP because clients open your PDF, but you might open the sheet in Google Sheets, LibreOffice or an older Excel, and all of them evaluate this one. A COUNTIF on the code column flags duplicates before they bite.

The totals block then reads Subtotal → Discount → Tax (only if a Yes/No setting says you collect it) → Total → Deposit to book → Remaining balance. The deposit line is =ROUND(Total * Setup!Deposit, 2) — the same cell the contract will quote.

Payment schedules fail because due dates are typed by hand. Compute them:

Add a late-fee estimate that is capped (MIN(overdue × rate × days, overdue × 5%)). A fee without a cap looks predatory in a dispute; a capped one is the number a mediator will accept.

The clause list that has held up for the vendors I have worked with, in order:

Then a one-page delivery and acceptance record. The signature on it starts the revision clock, which closes the "I only just looked at the gallery" conversation nine months later.

Walk the client through the checklist before sending the contract. Twenty clauses, two minutes on a call or a voice note. Clients sign faster when nothing in the document surprises them, and the vendors who do this report almost no disputes — not because the contract is tougher, but because expectations were set when everyone was still happy.

If you would rather not build this yourself, I packaged the workbook (7 sheets, 450+ formulas, zero macros) and the 11-section agreement as the Wedding Vendor Contract & Quotation Pack 2026 — English edition ($14, Excel + Word, works in Google Sheets/Docs). There is also an Indonesian-language edition with local tax and stamp-duty wording.

#9571. What is Blockchain: Everything You Need to Know (2022)

Imagine a world in which you can do transactions and many other things without having to give your personal information. A world in which you don’t need to rely on banks or governments anymore. Sounds amazing, right? That’s exactly what blockchain technology allows us to do.

It’s like your computer’s hard drive. blockchain is a technology that lets you store data in digital blocks, which are connected together like links in a chain.

Blockchain technology was originally invented in 1991 by two mathematicians, Stuart Haber and W. Scot Stornetta. They first proposed the system to ensure that timestamps could not be tampered with.

A few years later, in 1998, software developer Nick Szabo proposed using a similar kind of technology to secure a digital payments system he called “Bit Gold.” However, this innovation was not adopted until Satoshi Nakamoto claimed to have invented the first Blockchain and Bitcoin.

A blockchain is a distributed database shared between the nodes of a computer network. It saves information in digital format. Many people first heard of blockchain technology when they started to look up information about bitcoin.

Blockchain is used in cryptocurrency systems to ensure secure, decentralized records of transactions.

Blockchain allowed people to guarantee the fidelity and security of a record of data without the need for a third party to ensure accuracy.

To understand how a blockchain works, Consider these basic steps:

Let’s get to know more about the blockchain.

Blockchain records digital information and distributes it across the network without changing it. The information is distributed among many users and stored in an immutable, permanent ledger that can't be changed or destroyed. That's why blockchain is also called "Distributed Ledger Technology" or DLT.

And that’s the beauty of it! The process may seem complicated, but it’s done in minutes with modern technology. And because technology is advancing rapidly, I expect things to move even more quickly than ever.

Even though blockchain is integral to cryptocurrency, it has other applications. For example, blockchain can be used for storing reliable data about transactions. Many people confuse blockchain with cryptocurrencies like bitcoin and ethereum.

Blockchain already being adopted by some big-name companies, such as Walmart, AIG, Siemens, Pfizer, and Unilever. For example, IBM's Food Trust uses blockchain to track food's journey before reaching its final destination.

Although some of you may consider this practice excessive, food suppliers and manufacturers adhere to the policy of tracing their products because bacteria such as E. coli and Salmonella have been found in packaged foods. In addition, there have been isolated cases where dangerous allergens such as peanuts have accidentally been introduced into certain products.

Tracing and identifying the sources of an outbreak is a challenging task that can take months or years. Thanks to the Blockchain, however, companies now know exactly where their food has been—so they can trace its location and prevent future outbreaks.

Blockchain technology allows systems to react much faster in the event of a hazard. It also has many other uses in the modern world.

Blockchain technology is safe, even if it’s public. People can access the technology using an internet connection.

Have you ever been in a situation where you had all your data stored at one place and that one secure place got compromised? Wouldn't it be great if there was a way to prevent your data from leaking out even when the security of your storage systems is compromised?

Blockchain technology provides a way of avoiding this situation by using multiple computers at different locations to store information about transactions. If one computer experiences problems with a transaction, it will not affect the other nodes.

Instead, other nodes will use the correct information to cross-reference your incorrect node. This is called “Decentralization,” meaning all the information is stored in multiple places.

Blockchain guarantees your data's authenticity—not just its accuracy, but also its irreversibility. It can also be used to store data that are difficult to register, like legal contracts, state identifications, or a company's product inventory.

Blockchain has many advantages and disadvantages.

I’ll answer the most frequently asked questions about blockchain in this section.

Blockchain is not a cryptocurrency but a technology that makes cryptocurrencies possible. It's a digital ledger that records every transaction seamlessly.

Yes, blockchain can be theoretically hacked, but it is a complicated task to be achieved. A network of users constantly reviews it, which makes hacking the blockchain difficult.

Coinbase Global is currently the biggest blockchain company in the world. The company runs a commendable infrastructure, services, and technology for the digital currency economy.

Blockchain is a decentralized technology. It’s a chain of distributed ledgers connected with nodes. Each node can be any electronic device. Thus, one owns blockhain.

Bitcoin is a cryptocurrency, which is powered by Blockchain technology while Blockchain is a distributed ledger of cryptocurrency

Generally a database is a collection of data which can be stored and organized using a database management system. The people who have access to the database can view or edit the information stored there. The client-server network architecture is used to implement databases. whereas a blockchain is a growing list of records, called blocks, stored in a distributed system. Each block contains a cryptographic hash of the previous block, timestamp and transaction information. Modification of data is not allowed due to the design of the blockchain. The technology allows decentralized control and eliminates risks of data modification by other parties.

Blockchain has a wide spectrum of applications and, over the next 5-10 years, we will likely see it being integrated into all sorts of industries. From finance to healthcare, blockchain could revolutionize the way we store and share data. Although there is some hesitation to adopt blockchain systems right now, that won't be the case in 2022-2023 (and even less so in 2026). Once people become more comfortable with the technology and understand how it can work for them, owners, CEOs and entrepreneurs alike will be quick to leverage blockchain technology for their own gain. #9570. Day 3 never came. My son and I stopped racing and built a game engine.

In March, my son and I made a bet. 80 days. Build real software. Sell it. Father vs son, shipping every day.

We'd been racing each other. Breadth against depth. Me knocking on more doors, him polishing one thing until it shone.

Then we noticed something. We have different skills, and we think in different ways. What one of us lacks, the other brings.

And we'd both been making games and game engines for years. Separately.

So we stopped racing and started building together. Day 2 said we had to work smarter. This was it. Synergy turned out to be real.

Myth Engine is a game engine for 2D and 3D games. The games you make can run on the web, on desktop and on mobile. It's built with JavaScript and Babylon.js, and it uses ECS (entity component system), which makes putting a game together feel intuitive and helps games run fast.

You make games in the editor on Windows, with Visual Logic blocks, JavaScript, or both. The editor draws your level with the game's own runtime, so you see it as it will look in the game.

We didn't just build the engine. We made games with it.

2D and 3D games, shooters, puzzles, platformers, worlds made of blocks and science labs, all made in Myth Engine.

Every object is built from components that you add and tune. The same Object Editor builds 2D and 3D objects.

Game rules are Visual Logic blocks you connect: when something happens, such as a button press, do something. Build a behavior once and attach it to as many objects as you like.

Pause the game right before any block runs, step through it, and watch each object's values change.

JavaScript works instead of blocks or alongside them, with suggestions for your project's own objects and sounds as you type. JavaScript libraries can be added from a catalog, and they're bundled into your game.

Ready-made looks, from old film and Game Boy to thermal camera and comic-book print. Up to four can be combined.

Build new looks from connected blocks, or write them as code.

Particle effects in 2D and 3D, starting from presets such as fire, rain and confetti.

Generated worlds with hills, caves, ores and trees, and a map preview before you play. Block worlds can be built by hand too.

There's more in the full tour on itch.io: What Myth Engine can do.

The free version has no time limit. Exporting finished games needs the full version, which is a one-time purchase with no royalties.

Call this Day 3. It just took a little longer than a day.

Next time: blocks or code? We settled it the family way.

#9569. We Stopped Feeding LLMs Raw HTML: Cutting Agent Scraping Costs by 74% Across 10,000 Targets

Every AI agent demo looks the same. You pass a URL to a scraper, hand the returned text to a model, and get clean JSON back. It works beautifully — right up until you point it at the real internet.

We were building an autonomous agent to track enterprise GPU availability: H100, H200, and Blackwell server rentals across cloud providers, wholesale distributor dashboards, and secondary marketplace brokers. The goal was simple. Watch thousands of supply points, detect availability and price shifts, and flag them before competitors noticed.

It collapsed in four days. Not because the model was weak, but because the plumbing underneath it was naive. Three things broke at once.

Roughly 78% of our target portals sat behind Cloudflare Turnstile, DataDome, or Akamai. Headless Chromium containers looped on challenges until the concurrency pool drained into a wall of HTTP 403s. The agent wasn't slow. It was locked out.

Premium residential bandwidth runs $8 to $15 per gigabyte. Downloading hero images, web fonts, and analytics beacons across 10,000 hourly targets meant infrastructure cost more than the arbitrage margin we were chasing. A system that is profitable on paper and cash-negative in practice is not a product. It is an expensive hobby.

The lesson that reshaped the whole design: an agent cannot reason over data it cannot reach, and it cannot stay cheap if every fetch is a paid browser session.

Our original pipeline sent every request through a rotating proxy and a full headless render. That is paying premium prices to read public pages.

We replaced it with three tiers of escalation. The rule: escalate only when the previous tier actually fails.

Tier 0 — Direct HTTP/2 (free). An async request with browser-accurate TLS fingerprints. If the response is a 200 with no mitigation signatures, we take the payload and move on. Documentation endpoints, status feeds, older portals, sitemaps, and RSS all die here, at zero marginal cost.

Tier 2 — Bright Data Scraping Browser. Only about 14% of targets genuinely need client-side rendering: React and Vue dashboards that hydrate pricing tables over WebSockets after load. Instead of running Chromium locally, we connect to a cloud browser over CDP and block images, CSS, and fonts at the network interception layer before a single byte is downloaded.

That single decision — connect to a remote browser instead of spawning a local one — cut memory per worker from 640 MB to 38 MB, and it took fingerprint-based honeypots out of the equation entirely.

A 2.4 MB e-commerce page usually contains under 4 KB of useful data. We built a deterministic pre-processor with two stages.

Stage 1: JSON-LD harvester. Retailers expose schema.org product and price data for Google, so we read that first. About 320 tokens, zero LLM calls, no hallucination surface. If a valid schema exists, the model never runs at all.

The model receives structure, not noise. That is the difference between an extraction agent and an expensive random-text summarizer.

Benchmark: 10,000 bot-protected URLs over seven days, compared against a baseline of local Playwright plus generic rotating residential proxies.

Request success rate: 36.4% baseline, 99.4% with the tri-tier engine.

Median ingestion latency: 14.8 seconds down to 2.6 seconds.

Tokens per LLM call: 14,200 down to 1,650.

Cost per 10,000 operations: $184.20 down to $47.50.

The cost delta is the entire argument. At 100,000 daily checks, the naive stack burns roughly $1,842 a day before the model thinks once. Tri-tier routing is not a micro-optimization. It is the difference between a viable product and a money fire.

Production exposes what benchmarks hide. Three things we had to fix after launch.

Sticky session lockouts. Rotating IPs on every request invalidated multi-step carts and authenticated distributor portals. Fixed by pinning consistent session identifiers to the same residential exit node for the duration of a transaction.

Canvas fingerprinting. Newer anti-bot suites render interactive WebGL challenges that static scrapers cannot simulate. Offloading those specific endpoints to the cloud browser resolved it without touching the rest of the pipeline.

Failures that compound. Blind retries turned a single upstream outage into a request storm. Fixed with exponential backoff, jitter, and cached state snapshots so the agent degrades instead of collapsing.

The hard part of autonomous agents is not the prompt. It is the ingestion layer: reaching the data, paying the minimum for it, and delivering it clean enough that a model can reason about it without inventing things.

Treat extraction as production infrastructure, and your agent stops being a demo. Ignore it, and no amount of prompt engineering will save you — because the agent will be staring at a 403 page and hallucinating anyway.

#9568. How long does pie last in the fridge? : Because we're all wondering what to do with our apple and pumpkin pies.

The bakers of King Arthur are here to solve the kitchen conundrums you share with us, whether it’s on the phone, computer, or by the good old postal service. In Ask the Baker’s Hotline, Annabelle will pick the brains of the talented King Arthur Baker’s Hotline team to tackle some of your most-asked questions. Today: How long does pie last in the fridge?

The season of plentiful pies is upon us. When preparing several pies for a holiday meal, you may be wondering about the imminent leftovers. Should apple pie be stored differently than pumpkin pie? David from our Baker’s Hotline is here with his expert advice to help.

“Baked apple or other fruit pies can be kept covered, at room temperature, for one to two days. After that, they’ll keep in the fridge for one to two more days,” David advises. A 15-minute reheat in a 350°F oven can help revive some of that freshly baked flavor. Tent the pie with foil so it doesn’t brown further.

Interested in prepping ahead? David says that storing an assembled, ready-to-bake apple pie is a bad idea; the fruity filling will release moisture, which will make your crust soggy. Instead, roll out your pie crusts and prep your apples, but keep them separate. And wait to add the sugar and spices to the apples until you’re ready to bake the pie. This way, you can pour off any liquid that’s accumulated from the fruit without draining off your thickener, sugar, and spices.

Sliced apples turn brown, so you don’t want to keep your prepared apples in the fridge very long before baking. Aim for under 24 hours, but a squeeze of lemon juice could help them last another day or so.

And if you want to use your freezer to prep ahead, here’s how to freeze and bake fruit pies.

David advises, “Baked pumpkin pie or other pies containing eggs and/or dairy such as pecan pie, custard pie, or chiffon pie should be stored refrigerated; they’ll keep in the fridge for three to four days. I like to transfer the pie to a shallow, lidded storage container, but plastic wrap or a storage top can be used as well.”

As with apple, if you’re making your pumpkin (and other custard) pie ahead, it’s best to keep filling and crust separate. Pumpkin pie filling can be made ahead; it’ll keep, refrigerated, overnight. In fact, that's actually what we recommend doing; the custard develops incredible flavor and aroma as it sits.

If you can, serve pies the day they were made instead of refrigerating them.

Reheat refrigerated pies in a 350°F oven for about 15 minutes prior to serving.

Apple and other fruit pies will last at room temperature for up to two days, then in the fridge for two more.

Pumpkin, custard, or other egg/dairy-based pies can be stored in the fridge for up to four days.

If you’re making the crust and the filling ahead, keep them separated until it’s time to bake your pie.

Get more tips for holiday success in our Thanksgiving Baking Guide.

#9566. Claude config: rules and guardrails for Claude Code on .NET + Angular projects

I work on .NET and Angular projects with Claude Code. For every new project I kept writing the same instructions again: which stack to use, how to handle Git, what Claude must never do on its own, how to ask questions. So I put all of it in one place: claude-config, a public template of rules plus a small Claude Code plugin.

Repository: https://github.com/AngeloDotNet/claude-config

Claude Code loads the files under .claude/rules/ by itself, so the rules are copied into each project and nothing is installed globally. The modules are:

Optional modules (email, infrastructure, feature workflow) live in .claude/rules-optional/ and are switched on only when a project needs them.

The rules are written in Italian, because that is the language I work in, while code, identifiers and commit messages stay in English. You can change that to suit your own team.

A few of the rules in core.md shape almost every session:

Written rules are only a suggestion, so the plugin turns the most important ones into hooks:

The documentation covers three situations:

The CLAUDE.md in each project holds only what is specific to that project. Choices such as architecture, ORM, database, multi-tenancy or the ASVS level are never assumed: the template asks for them and they are recorded once. The copia-regole.bat script copies the rules and root files into a project folder and can update the rules already present.

This is my own opinionated setup, not a universal standard. Some details are not yet verified against their sources, and the changelog says so openly. For example, the exact PostgreSQL row-level security syntax and passkey support in ASP.NET Core Identity on .NET 10 are marked to be checked the first time they are used. Treat the rules as a starting point and adapt them to your projects.

If you try it on a real project, I would like to hear what breaks first.

#9564. Most Frequently Asked Questions About Affiliate Marketing

Affiliate marketing is a way to make money by promoting the products and services of other people and companies. You don't need to create your product or service, just promote existing ones. That's why it's so easy to get started with affiliate marketing. You can even get started with no budget at all!

An affiliate program is a package of information you create for your product, which is then made available to potential publishers. The program will typically include details about the product and its retail value, commission levels, and promotional materials. Many affiliate programs are managed via an affiliate network like ShareASale, which acts as a platform to connect publishers and advertisers, but it is also possible to offer your program directly.

Affiliate networks connect publishers to advertisers.  Affiliate networks make money by charging fees to the merchants who advertise with them; these merchants are known as advertisers. The percentage of each sale that the advertiser pays is negotiated between the merchant and the affiliate network.

Dropshipping is a method of selling that allows you to run an online store without having to stock products. You advertise the products as if you owned them, but when someone makes an order, you create a duplicate order with the distributor at a reduced price. The distributor takes care of the post and packaging on your behalf. As affiliate marketing is based on referrals and this type of drop shipping requires no investment in inventory when a customer buys through the affiliate link, no money exchanges hands.

Performance marketing is a method of marketing that pays for performance, like when a sale is made or an ad is clicked This can include methods like PPC (pay-per-click) or display advertising. Affiliate marketing is one form of performance marketing where commissions are paid out to affiliates on a performance basis when they click on their affiliate link and make a purchase or action.

Smartphones are essentially miniature computers, so publishers can display the same websites and offers that are available on a PC. But mobiles also offer specific tools not available on computers, and these can be used to good effect for publishers. Publishers can optimize their ads for mobile users by making them easy to access by this audience. Publishers can also make good use of text and instant messaging to promote their offers. As the mobile market is predicted to make up 80% of traffic in the future, publishers who do not promote on mobile devices are missing out on a big opportunity.

The best way to find affiliate publishers is on reputable networks like ShareASale Cj(Commission Junction), Awin, and Impact radius. These networks have a strict application process and compliance checks, which means that all affiliates are trustworthy.

An affiliate disclosure statement discloses to the reader that there may be affiliate links on a website, for which a commission may be paid to the publisher if visitors follow these links and make purchases.

Publishers promote their programs through a variety of means, including blogs, websites, email marketing, and pay-per-click ads. Social media has a huge interactive audience, making this platform a good source of potential traffic.

A super affiliate is an affiliate partner who consistently drives a large majority of sales from any program they promote, compared to other affiliate partners involved in that program.  Affiliates make a lot of money from affiliate marketing Pat Flynn earned more than $50000 in 2013 from affiliate marketing.

Because the Internet is so widespread, affiliate programs can be promoted in any country. Affiliate strategies that are set internationally need to be tailored to the language of the targeted country.

Affiliate marketing can help you grow your business in the following ways:

One of the best ways to work with qualified affiliates is to hire an affiliate marketing agency that works with all the networks. Affiliates are carefully selected and go through a rigorous application process to be included in the network.

Affiliate marketing is generally associated with websites, but there are other ways to promote your affiliate links, including:

To build your affiliate marketing business, you don't have to invest money in the beginning. You can sign up for free with any affiliate network and start promoting their brands right away.

Commission rates are typically based on a percentage of the total sale and in some cases can also be a flat fee for each transaction. The rates are set by the merchant.

Some merchants run their affiliate programs internally, while others choose to contract out management to a network or an external agency.

#9563. Stop Trusting Notification URLs

Hichem Hannafi is a Las Vegas–based technology entrepreneur with over 13 years of experience driving software innovation.

Hichem Hannafi is a Las Vegas–based technology entrepreneur with over 13 years of experience driving software innovation.

Hichem Hannafi is a Las Vegas–based technology entrepreneur with over 13 years of experience driving software innovation.

TL;DR: Every bid response a DSP sends carries URLs that anyone who has seen the response can call: impression, click, win, billing. Most DSPs count whatever comes in, which is where discrepancy reports come from. We treated a notification URL like a cheque: valid only if we issued it, for that bid, and it hasn’t been cashed. The bidder mints hashes and a spend reservation at bid time; every callback is checked against them, duplicates and replays are rejected, and unclaimed reservations expire after 45 minutes. Result: about 6% of callbacks rejected as unverifiable, and reported impressions within 1% of the exchanges’ figures.

Every bid response a DSP sends contains a set of URLs: call this one when the ad is shown, this one when it is clicked, this one when the auction is won, this one when it is billed. The exchange, the publisher’s page, and anyone else who has seen the response can call them. Most DSPs count whatever comes in.

That is the quiet reason discrepancy reports exist. Not fraud, usually, though fraud rides along happily. Mostly it is duplicate calls, replayed calls, calls from cached responses that never rendered, and callbacks for auctions the DSP did not win. Every one of them becomes an impression in a report, a dollar in an invoice, and an argument with an advertiser.

When I built the bidder for Mobinner’s DSP, I treated a notification URL the way a bank treats a cheque: it is only good if we issued it, for that amount, and it has not been cashed already.

The mechanism is simple. When a bidder node decides to bid, it does three things before it responds. It reserves the bid amount against the campaign budget in a shared store, so that parallel nodes cannot spend the same dollar twice. It generates a set of hashes, one for the conversion and one for each tracking event, and stores them alongside the reservation. And it embeds those hashes in the notification URLs it returns.

When a callback arrives, the handler does not count it. It looks up the hashes for that bid and compares. If they match, the event is written to reporting, the hash is cleared so the same event cannot be counted twice, and the spend is committed. If they do not match, or there is no reservation, the call is rejected, and nothing is recorded. If no callback ever arrives, the reservation expires after 45 minutes, and a cleaner service returns the budget to the campaign; conversion hashes live 48 hours, because conversions arrive late.

The result is that a notification URL has no value to anyone except the winner of the bid it was issued for, and that nothing reaches a report unless it was bid for, won, and seen once.

A write to the shared store on every bid, and a read on every callback. That is not free at scale, and it is the reason some DSPs skip it: the bid path is where milliseconds matter, and a store round trip is a visible cost. We judged it worth paying, because the alternative is reconciling discrepancies by hand every month, which costs more and never ends. In a typical month, we rejected roughly 6% of incoming callbacks as unverifiable, and our reported impressions came within 1% of the exchanges’ own figures.

Three things have changed since this design was new. Supply-path optimisation means a DSP sees the same impression through several paths, and duplicate callbacks are a feature of the plumbing, not a bug. Server-side rendering and prefetching mean more responses are generated than are ever shown. And the gap between a bid and its billing notice is where most of the money in programmatic goes missing.

A DSP that counts callbacks on trust is making a promise to advertisers it cannot keep. The fix is not a fraud vendor bolted on afterwards; it is refusing, at the point of counting, to count anything you did not issue.

Ask your DSP one question: if I call your impression URL twice, what happens? If the answer is anything other than “the second call is rejected,” you are paying for the second call.

Hichem Hannafi is a Las Vegas–based technology entrepreneur with over 13 years of experience driving software innovation.

#9562. Measuring Calls and Forms Before A/B Testing a Law Firm Site

If you build or maintain sites for criminal defense firms, someone will eventually ask you to "run an A/B test" on a charge page. Before you pick a tool, check whether the site can measure the thing the firm cares about. On most defense sites that is a phone call from a mobile visitor, and a surprising number of sites record it poorly or not at all.

Testing without reliable conversion data produces confident charts about nothing. This post covers the measurement groundwork that should be in place first, with notes on the constraints that make legal sites different from ecommerce.

Developers often default to whatever the analytics tool tracks automatically. For a defense firm that is the wrong starting point. Sit down with whoever runs intake and agree on what counts:

Then agree on which of those count as primary. Many firms care far more about calls than forms. Write the definitions down, because six months later nobody will remember whether chat openings were included.

Google Optimize was shut down on September 30, 2023, so many teams now pair GA4 with a separate testing tool or run server-side experiments. Whatever you choose, the conversion events have to exist in analytics first.

GA4 has a recommended event called generate_lead for form submissions. Phone taps need a custom event. A minimal version looks like this:

Fire the form event only after the server confirms the submission. Firing on button click counts failed validations and double taps. Add a data attribute to each phone link so you can tell header taps from in-content taps, which matters when the test changes where the number appears.

Google Analytics policies prohibit sending personally identifiable information, and a defense intake form collects some of the most sensitive data a website can hold: names, phone numbers, charges, arrest dates. None of it should reach analytics, a heat map tool or a session recorder.

Check a few things before any test goes live. Form fields should be excluded or masked in any recording tool. URLs should not carry form values as query strings after submission. Event parameters should describe the form, never its contents. If the firm uses a third-party form service, confirm where submissions are stored and who can see them.

A phone_tap event shows intent. It does not prove a call connected. Call tracking with dynamic number insertion can close that gap by showing a different number per source and logging calls on the provider's side. If you use it, keep the firm's main number consistent in the footer, schema markup and Google Business Profile so local search signals stay clean.

The richest data lives in intake. A short field asking how the caller found the firm, plus a weekly export, lets you compare test variants on signed cases rather than raw contacts. For the form side of that work, designing an intake form a frightened caller will finish covers how many fields to ask for and how to word labels for a scared person typing on a phone.

Most defense charge pages see modest traffic and few conversions. Run the numbers before you promise a result. If a page produces twenty calls a month, a split test chasing a ten percent lift will take far longer than anyone will wait.

With small numbers, test large changes to the first mobile screen, run variants for fixed periods and keep a change log in the repo. Before and after comparisons are weaker evidence than a true split, but they are often the only realistic option, and they are fine if you say so in the report.

Each variant is attorney advertising. If a test changes headlines, claims or disclaimers, the firm's lawyers need to approve it, and state bar advertising rules apply to every version a visitor might see. Build the approval step into your deployment process so a variant cannot ship by accident.

More on testing ideas for legal sites is collected in the conversion testing library for law firm websites.

Mark them as key events if the firm treats calls as its main goal. Report them separately from forms so changes in one do not hide changes in the other.

Only with strict masking of every input and a review of where recordings are stored. Many firms decide the risk is not worth it.

Pick one that works with your stack and supports server-side or flicker-free variants. The tool matters less than clean conversion data and an honest sample size.

SBD Marketing works only with criminal defense firms, one firm per city. It builds websites for defense practices, handles SEO for the charges a firm defends, works on visibility in AI search tools and runs SEO audits.

#9561. 51 Thanksgiving dessert recipes for a sweet holiday: From cookies to cake — and of course, plenty of pie.

Of course, we had to start with pumpkin pie. This is a rich, well-spiced pie, thanks to a powerful punch of ginger, cinnamon, nutmeg, cloves, and black pepper. Two hints for a better result: Mix the filling a day in advance to give the spices a chance to bloom, and be sure to remove the pie from the oven while the center is still wobbly, as overcooking it will cause the filling to crack.

Want even more spice in your pumpkin pie? This spice-forward recipe is for you. Using powerful Vietnamese cinnamon — with its more robust flavor profile — gives the pie an even spicier kick. Meanwhile, the filling is super silky-smooth thanks to a few tablespoons of corn syrup mixed in.

Get the recipe: Smooth and Spicy Pumpkin Pie

With its retro vibe, this play on classic chiffon pie is noteworthy for its tender rye crust and its bright, light chiffon filling. The zesty cranberry curd and smooth, sweet Swiss meringue play beautifully together. And the gelatin helps the filling set just right so that once refrigerated, the pie can be sliced neatly. Tart and airy, this pie is an excellent counterpoint to a heavy feast.

Shop the recipe: Organic Medium Rye Flour

Intimidated by pie? Don't be! Our guide on How to Bake Pie has everything you need for a successful, stress-free bake.

This double-crusted beauty is generously filled with sweet-tart apples and spiced with cinnamon, nutmeg, and allspice. But the real secret to its flavorful filling is boiled cider, one of our favorite fall ingredients. The sticky tart-sweet syrup adds an extra depth of apple flavor to make this classic pie stand out from the crowd.

Shop the recipe: Vermont Boiled Cider and Instant ClearJel

This unusual method for baking apple pie caught our eye years ago, when a reader sent it via e-mail. But it’s not just a stunt: Baking a pie in a paper grocery bag gives you a beautifully golden brown, perfectly cooked pie, with toothsome yet tender apples (which soften better thanks to the steam trapped by the bag) beneath a streusel topping.

This beloved pie is made much like pumpkin pie, but with mashed sweet potatoes for nuanced flavor and heavy cream for an especially rich custard. Top it with toasted molasses meringue (if you want the pie to be reminiscent of the classic yams and marshmallow dish served at Thanksgiving), or for a simpler option, with freshly whipped cream. (And for a more unconventional version, try this striking Purple Sweet Potato Pie.)

This traditional pie doesn’t use corn syrup — instead, it’s sweetened entirely with brown sugar. The filling is silky smooth, and the pecans on top toast nicely as the pie bakes. Be sure to use high-quality vanilla extract for well-rounded flavor; an optional handful of chopped bittersweet chocolate is a nice addition, too.

If you’re intimidated by pie (or just don’t have time to chill and roll out pie dough) this easier version of pecan pie is for you. A buttery, brown-sugar shortbread crust cradles a gooey honey-sweetened pecan filling. These bars keep well for days, so they’re perfect for baking ahead of Thanksgiving.

This recipe takes classic pecan pie a step further by adding chocolate chips to the filling. The chocolate beautifully complements the pecans' nuttiness; if you choose bittersweet chocolate, it cuts the pie's overall sweetness, allowing all of the flavors to shine more brightly.

Shop the recipe: Guittard Bittersweet Chocolate Chips

Baker's tip: Make and freeze your pie crust early to get ahead on pie prep.

This creamy, decadent pie is positively bursting with maple flavor — be sure to use the best maple syrup you can find and a dash of natural maple flavor to enhance it. One bite of the brûléed maple sugar top and the silky-smooth filling will have you reconsidering your regular rotation of cream pies this Thanksgiving.

Shop the recipe: Vermont Maple Syrup and Natural Maple Flavor

These handheld treats harness all the nostalgia of a steaming hot McDonald’s fried apple pie but are infinitely better, thanks to homemade flaky pie crust, a fresh apple filling amplified by boiled cider, and a generous coating of cinnamon sugar. If you’re only in charge of dessert this year and want to flex a little, this recipe is an impressive (and tasty!) way to do so.

Shop the recipe: Boiled Cider and Apple Pie Spice

Mash-up pies are an easy way to please your guests without making multiple pies. This recipe has the best of both worlds: a smooth layer of spiced pumpkin custard plus a rich pecan topping. It’s best made a day ahead so that the flavors can settle, plus there’s one less dish to worry about on Thanksgiving Day.

Shop the recipe: Adjustable Pie Crust Shield

Is there anything cuter than a mini Thanksgiving pie? Filled with a pre-cooked, perfectly spiced filling that’s enhanced with tart boiled cider, these bite-sized treats can be topped with a woven lattice or streusel.

This tart-sweet cake is easy to throw together — made with melted butter, the one-bowl batter is mixed by hand then poured directly over sugared cranberries. If you have cranberries leftover from making sauce or just want to highlight these seasonal berries in other ways, make this cake.

Shop the recipe: Pure Almond Extract and Sparkling Sugar

This stunning pumpkin swirl cake is more than just good looks: It also has a soft, plush texture, thanks to cake flour and sour cream, and a deep pumpkin flavor paired with fragrant vanilla. It starts with one base batter that gets flavored two ways, creating two distinct colors for a striking visual contrast when sliced.

For a more traditional dessert, try this pumpkin-y layer cake. It’s moist and slightly dense from the pumpkin purée, with a tangy cream cheese frosting and sticky caramel glaze.

Get the recipe: Pumpkin Layer Cake with Cream Cheese Frosting

In this unabashedly apple-forward apple cake, there are so many apple slices and so little batter, you’ll wonder how (and if) it will hold together. But never fear: As the batter rises in the oven, it knits those slices together to create a tender cake that’s almost creamy and custardy due to the abundance of fruit.

Shop the recipe: Almond Flour and Pure Almond Extract

The pumpkin and pumpkin-friendly spices (cloves, cinnamon, allspice) in this cake meld surprisingly well with the chocolate chips studded throughout. This dark, moist Bundt cake is rich enough to serve unfrosted, and it's just the ticket when you want to serve a dessert that's substantial, yet not too sweet, to finish your Thanksgiving meal. And it keeps well for days, so you can bake it early in the week to help prep ahead.

#9558. TOP 11 AI MARKETING TOOLS YOU SHOULD USE (Updated 2022)

  

 The marketing industry is turning to artificial intelligence (AI) as a way to save time and execute smarter, more personalized campaigns. 61% of marketers say AI software is the most important aspect of their data strategy.

  If you’re late to the AI party, don’t worry. It’s easier than you think to start leveraging artificial intelligence tools in your marketing strategy. Here are 11 AI marketing tools every marketer should start using today.

1. Jasper Ai(Formerly known as Jarvis)


Jasper is a content writing and content generation tool that uses artificial intelligence to identify the best words and sentences for your writing style and medium in the most efficient, quick, and accessible way.

Key Features

  •  It's trusted by 50,000+ marketers for creating engaging marketing campaigns, ad copy, blog posts, and articles within minutes which would traditionally take hours or days. Special Features:
  • Blog posts have been optimized for search engines and rank high on Google and other search engines. This is a huge plus for online businesses that want to generate traffic to their website through content marketing.
  • 99.9% Original Content and guarantees that all content it generates will be original, so businesses can focus on their online reputation rather than worrying about penalties from Google for duplicate content.
  • Long-Form Article Writing – Jasper.ai is also useful for long-form writing, allowing users to create articles of up to 10,000 words without any difficulty. This is ideal for businesses that want to produce in-depth content that will capture their audience’s attention.

2. Personalize

 Personalize is an AI-powered technology that helps you identify and produce highly targeted sales and marketing campaigns by tracking the products and services your contacts are most interested in at any given time. The platform uses an algorithm to identify each contact’s top three interests, which are updated in real-time based on recent site activity.

Key Features

  • Identifies  top three interests based on metrics like time on page, recency, and frequency of each contact
  • Works with every ESP and CRM
  • Easy to get up and running in days
  • Enterprise-grade technology at a low cost for SMBs

3. Seventh Sense

  Seventh Sense provides behavioral analytics that helps you win attention in your customers’ overcrowded email inboxes. Choosing the best day and time to send an email is always a gamble. And while some days of the week generally get higher open rates than others, you’ll never be able to nail down a time that’s best for every customer. Seventh Sense eases your stress of having to figure out the perfect send-time and day for your email campaigns. The AI-based platform figures out the best timing and email frequency for each contact based on when they’re opening emails. The tool is primarily geared toward HubSpot and Marketo customers 

Key Features 

  • AI determines the best send-time and email frequency for each contact
  • Connects with HubSpot and Marketo

4. Phrasee

  Phrasee uses artificial intelligence to help you write more effective subject lines. With its AI-based Natural Language Generation system, Phrasee uses data-driven insights to generate millions of natural-sounding copy variants that match your brand voice. The model is end-to-end, meaning when you feed the results back to Phrasee, the prediction model rebuilds so it can continuously learn from your audience.

Key Features 

  • Instantly generates millions of human-sounding, brand-compliant copy variants
  • Creates tailored language models for every customer
  • Learns what your audience responds to and rebuilds the prediction model every time

5. Hubspot Seo

  HubSpot Search Engine Optimization (SEO) is an integral tool for the Human Content team. It uses machine learning to determine how search engines understand and categorize your content. HubSpot SEO helps you improve your search engine rankings and outrank your competitors. Search engines reward websites that organize their content around core subjects, or topic clusters. HubSpot SEO helps you discover and rank for the topics that matter to your business and customers.

Key Features 

  • Helps you discover and rank topics that people are searching for
  • Provides suggestions for your topic clusters and related subjects
  • Integrates with all other HubSpot content tools to help you create a well-rounded content strategy

 6. Evolve AI

  When you’re limited to testing two variables against each other at a time, it can take months to get the results you’re looking for. Evolv AI lets you test all your ideas at once. It uses advanced algorithms to identify the top-performing concepts, combine them with each other, and repeat the process to achieve the best site experience.

Key Features 

  • Figures out which content provides the best performance
  • Lets you test multiple ideas in a single experiment instead of having to perform many individual tests over a long period
  • Lets you try all your ideas across multiple pages for full-funnel optimization
  • Offers visual and code editors

7. Acrolinx

  Acrolinx is a content alignment platform that helps brands scale and improves the quality of their content. It’s geared toward enterprises – its major customers include big brands like Google, Adobe, and Amazon - to help them scale their writing efforts. Instead of spending time chasing down and fixing typos in multiple places throughout an article or blog post, you can use Acrolinx to do it all right there in one place. You start by setting your preferences for style, grammar, tone of voice, and company-specific word usage. Then, Acrolinx checks and scores your existing content to find what’s working and suggest areas for improvement. The platform provides real-time guidance and suggestions to make writing better and strengthen weak pages.

Key features

  • Reviews and scores existing content to ensure it meets your brand guidelines
  • Finds opportunities to improve your content and use automation to shorten your editorial process.
  • Integrates with more than 50 tools and platforms, including Google Docs, Microsoft Word, WordPress, and most web browsers.

8. MarketMuse 

MarketMuse uses an algorithm to help marketers build content strategies. The tool shows you where to target keywords to rank in specific topic categories, and recommends keywords you should go after if you want to own particular topics. It also identifies gaps and opportunities for new content and prioritizes them by their probable impact on your rankings. The algorithm compares your content with thousands of articles related to the same topic to uncover what’s missing from your site.

Key features:

  • The built-in editor shows how in-depth your topic is covered and what needs improvement
  • Finds gaps and opportunities for new content creation, prioritized by their probable impact and your chance of ranking

9. Copilot

Copilot is a suite of tools that help eCommerce businesses maintain real-time communication with customers around the clock at every stage of the funnel. Promote products, recover shopping carts and send updates or reminders directly through Messenger.

Key features: 

  • Integrate Facebook Messenger directly with your website, including chat history and recent interactions for a fluid customer service experience 
  • Run drip messenger campaigns to keep customers engaged with your brand
  • Send abandoned carts, out-of-stock, restock, preorder, order status, and shipment notifications to contacts 
  • Send branded images, promotional content, or coupon codes to those who opt in
  • Collect post-purchase feedback, reviews, and customer insight
  • Demonstrate social proof on your website with a widget, or push automatic Facebook posts sharing recent purchases
  • Display a promotional banner on your website to capture contacts instantly

10. Yotpo

Yotpo’s deep learning technology evaluates your customers’ product reviews to help you make better business decisions. It identifies key topics that customers mention related to your products—and their feelings toward them. The AI engine extracts relevant reviews from past buyers and presents them in smart displays to convert new shoppers. Yotpo also saves you time moderating reviews. The AI-powered moderation tool automatically assigns a score to each review and flags reviews with negative sentiment so you can focus on quality control instead of manually reviewing every post.

Key features:

  • Makes it easy for shoppers to filter reviews and find the exact information they’re looking for
  • Analyzes customer feedback and sentiments to help you improve your products
  • Integrates with most leading eCommerce platforms, including BigCommerce, Magento, and Shopify.

11. Albert AI

  Albert is a self-learning software that automates the creation of marketing campaigns for your brand. It analyzes vast amounts of data to run optimized campaigns autonomously, allowing you to feed in your own creative content and target markets, and then use data from its database to determine key characteristics of a serious buyer. Albert identifies potential customers that match those traits, and runs trial campaigns on a small group of customers—with results refined by Albert himself—before launching it on a larger scale.

  Albert plugs into your existing marketing technology stack, so you still have access to your accounts, ads, search, social media, and more. Albert maps tracking and attribution to your source of truth so you can determine which channels are driving your business.

Key features:

  • Breaks down large amounts of data to help you customize campaigns
  • Plugs into your marketing technology stack and can be used across diverse media outlets, including email, content, paid media, and mobile

Final Saying

There are many tools and companies out there that offer AI tools, but this is a small list of resources that we have found to be helpful. If you have any other suggestions, feel free to share them in the comments below this article. As marketing evolves at such a rapid pace, new marketing strategies will be invented that we haven't even dreamed of yet. But for now, this list should give you a good starting point on your way to implementing AI into your marketing mix.

#9556. Giving a macOS App Group Its Own Dock Icon: Design Lessons From Cybokron Dock Groups

Developer of Cybokron Dock Groups, a free and open-source macOS utility. https://cybokron.com/dock-groups/

Developer of Cybokron Dock Groups, a free and open-source macOS utility. https://cybokron.com/dock-groups/

Developer of Cybokron Dock Groups, a free and open-source macOS utility. https://cybokron.com/dock-groups/

A group of applications is easy to describe and surprisingly awkward to represent in a desktop interface. A developer might need an editor, a terminal, and a browser together, yet the Dock presents them as separate applications. Cybokron Dock Groups treats that collection as a named unit: something that can have its own icon, open its members, or hide them together. The interesting engineering problem is not the list of apps. It is making the group fit macOS without pretending it is a separate desktop session.

Disclosure: I am Ercan Atay, the developer of Cybokron Dock Groups, and have a direct interest in the project. This article was prepared with AI drafting assistance based on the project's public documentation. It is a developer's technical explanation, not an independent product review.

Consider a hypothetical Development group containing an editor, a terminal, a browser, and a documentation website. Opening that group should have a narrow, predictable meaning. It should launch applications that are closed, bring running applications forward, and open the website in the default browser.

It should not imply that a terminal command will resume, that a browser tab will return to a specific state, or that every window will move to a particular display. Those are different problems. Keeping that boundary explicit avoids promising a workspace-restoration system when the underlying object is a collection of launch targets.

The same distinction matters for ending work. Hide All hides only running member applications; it does not launch closed ones. Close All asks the group's running applications to quit normally. Force quit is a separate action, available through Command-click. It is not interchangeable with hiding, and it can discard unsaved work.

That gives the group a small vocabulary rather than a vague “switch workspace” command. The vocabulary is easier to explain because each action has a separate consequence.

A group can live in a menu-bar menu, but a persistent Dock entry needs something macOS can recognize. Cybokron's standalone mode creates a small application bundle for each group.

The bundle lives under the user's Application Support directory. It contains a copy of the project's executable, its own Info.plist, a group-specific bundle identifier, a group-config.json resource, and the group's icon. The executable runs in an agent role rather than creating another full menu-bar instance.

This is not just an alias to a list. The group has an application identity that can be registered with LaunchServices. Clicking its Dock icon toggles the popup; Option-click opens the group's members. The standalone agent can do this even when the main menu-bar app is not running.

There is a cost to that independence. A changed group needs its generated bundle updated, and a running agent needs to reload its configuration. A renamed group also needs its bundle path and Dock entry updated. The project repository documents these mechanics, including ad hoc signing and verification of the generated agents. These generated bundles should not be confused with the Developer ID-signed main application.

Adding a generated application to the Dock means changing persistent Dock entries. In this implementation, the Dock briefly restarts to display the change. That is a real side effect, not something a utility should conceal behind a claim of seamlessness.

The project keeps backups of the Dock's application list before writing it and retains the newest six. If it cannot read the existing list, it does not rewrite the Dock or disable groups on that basis. This is an important failure boundary: inability to understand an existing user configuration should not become permission to replace it.

The broader lesson is to design the failure path alongside the feature. A Dock icon is convenient, but preserving the user's existing Dock is more important than successfully adding one more item.

Apple's NSWorkspace documentation describes native facilities for launching applications and opening URLs. Those facilities are useful building blocks, but they do not make every piece of desktop interaction permission-free.

Cybokron asks for Accessibility access for global keyboard shortcuts, restoring minimized windows, and positioning a popup relative to its Dock icon. Without that permission, the remaining functionality is still available. Its global shortcuts are observed rather than consumed, so the foreground application also receives the key press.

That last detail is a trade-off worth stating plainly. A shortcut that works globally can still interact with the application currently in front. Users need to be able to change or disable it, not merely accept a hard-coded combination.

The same group operations are available through the cybokrondockgroups URL scheme. With a group named Work already configured, these examples show the distinction between displaying it and launching its members:

Apple's guide to using app URL schemes in Shortcuts explains how this kind of interface can connect an app to a larger workflow.

But a command URL is not equivalent to a private button. Another application or webpage can invoke it. Cybokron therefore asks for confirmation before a quit request, while launch and hide links share a five-second rate limit. These controls reduce specific accidental or repeated actions; they are not a claim that every possible external-input risk has disappeared.

Groups, settings, and usage counts stay in the user's Library folder. There is no account requirement or analytics service. However, the application does contact GitHub for release checks, release notes, and update downloads. Describing it as entirely offline would be inaccurate.

Update verification is also more than comparing a version string. The documented checks include the download's size and SHA-256, with Developer ID builds additionally requiring the expected signing identity. Older ad hoc-signed releases have a weaker trust boundary, so that distinction belongs in technical documentation rather than being flattened into a universal security claim.

The product page describes a free, MIT-licensed utility for macOS 14 and later, supporting Apple Silicon and Intel. The reusable idea is narrower than a feature list: make the group a recognizable native object, distinguish actions with different consequences, and expose the limits of permissions, persistence, and external commands. That is a useful design checklist even for a developer who never installs this particular utility.

Disclosure: I develop Cybokron Dock Groups and have a direct interest in it. AI assisted the preparation of this article. No independent testing or benchmark results are claimed here.

Developer of Cybokron Dock Groups, a free and open-source macOS utility. https://cybokron.com/dock-groups/

#9554. 17 apple dessert recipes for fall baking: Embrace the season with apple tarts, cookies, cakes, and more.

There’s an apple dessert for everyone. For the purists, there are lattice-topped pies and shingled galettes. For the non-traditionalists, there are caramel-frosted cakes and fritter-inspired loaves. And for apple lovers that hate cinnamon? Well, there are custardy cakes and classic French tarts. Ready to start baking with fall’s best fruit? Read on for our best apple dessert recipes.

There’s no shortage of apple in this cake — applesauce keeps things moist while boiled cider adds sharp, tangy fruit flavor. The cake is great on its own, but pair it with light, creamy Whipped Caramel Frosting, and you’ve got an irresistible baked version of a caramel apple (with none of the fears about your teeth).

Get the recipe: Whipped Caramel Apple Cake

To make this recipe, you'll need: Vermont Boiled Cider

You only need one apple (and two people eager for an apple dessert) to make a pair of these adorable galettes. Half the apple is sliced, while the other half is grated, which creates a hidden layer of jam beneath the shingled slices. Flaky fruit tarts don’t get easier (or cuter!) than this.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Apple Pie Spice

Get the recipe: Apple Cider Snickerdoodles

This super-easy one-bowl cake is loaded with chopped apples and walnuts, which give this moist, spiced cake heft and texture. The frosting, akin to a velvety brown sugar fudge, adds a textural counterpoint and an extra dimension of richness.

Get the recipe: Old-Fashioned Apple Cake with Brown Sugar Frosting

To make this recipe, you'll need: 9" x 13" pan

Cinnamon and apple go together like a flannel and a beanie, but this recipe one-ups that perfect pairing with the addition of cinnamon chips. Diced apple and melty pockets of cinnamon-sugar are also studded throughout these autumnal scones, which are then finished off with an extra-crunchy sugar coating.

Get the recipe: Fresh Apple Cinnamon Scones

To make this recipe, you'll need: Cinnamon Sweet Bits

Ribbons of gooey, cinnamon-scented apples are twisted throughout this striking enriched loaf. Beautiful to behold (and easier to make than you’d think), this braided babka would be a welcome addition to any Rosh Hashanah table or fall celebration.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Baker’s Special Dry Milk

Spoiler alert: The eponymous secret ingredient in this special pie is boiled cider! Made by cooking down apple cider into a concentrate, a few drops deliver big apple flavor. When used in apple pies, it super-charges the fruit’s tart, tangy flavor, delivering a pie with over-the-top apple goodness.

Get the recipe: Secret Ingredient Apple Pie

To make this recipe, you'll need: Boiled Cider

If your go-to doughnut order is an apple fritter, this mash-up cake was made for you. The batter is made using the reverse creaming technique, which ensures a velvety crumb and tender texture. In each slice, there’s a filling and topping of cinnamon-dusted apples and a final drizzle of icy-white vanilla glaze. A slice rivals anything you can get at your local doughnut shop.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Instant ClearJel

This time of year, apples don't need much to make them shine. The paper-thin, crackly top layer of this cobbler highlights the juicy fruit beneath. It doesn’t need a lot of adornment, but a scoop of vanilla ice cream never hurt anything.

Get the recipe: Sugar-Crusted Apple Cobbler Cake

To make this recipe, you'll need: Vietnamese Cinnamon

Is it a bar? A slab pie? Both! This breezy recipe swaps the flaky pastry for a buttery shortbread crust but keeps the warm, gooey apples and classic spices for a sliceable, portable dessert. To finish, there's a crumbly streusel topping inspired by Dutch apple pie.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Apple Pie Spice

When you want a fruit dessert fast, you can always count on crisps — no rolling, no resting, and most importantly, no special equipment required! This crisp is made with a handful of baking basics, so when you find yourself with a surplus of apples, dessert is barely an hour away.

To make this recipe, you'll need: 9" Square Pan

Beneath a buttery, apple-pie-spiced streusel lies a generous layer of tender apples, enriched with intensely flavored boiled cider for a filling that tastes like a truly great apple pie — rich, saucy, and fork-tender apples. The sour cream cake that surrounds the apple filling is plush, subtly tangy, and ultra-moist, providing the perfect counterpoint to the fruit filling and crumb topping.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Apple Pie Spice

If you’re looking to veer from classic apple pie territory, this galette stays true to those roots but adds a few modern twists. It starts with a buttery whole wheat crust enriched with a touch of sour cream. Then, a layer of apple butter (which can be easily made by cooking down applesauce) is spread beneath a layer of artfully arranged apples slices.

Get the recipe: Apple Butter Apple Galette

To make this recipe, you'll need: Sparkling Sugar

There’s just enough batter to hold together a heap of sliced apples in this one-of-a-kind cake. Gently sweetened with brown sugar and scented with almond extract, this minimalist cake is greater than the sum of its parts — a sophisticated, custardy cake that’s deceivingly simple to make.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Almond Extract

This pull-apart bread is as fun to make as it is to eat. After rolling out the dough into a rectangle, it’s spread with sweetened apple filling. The dough is cut up into several strips, then stacked and squeezed into a loaf pan. It bakes into a loaf comprised of distinct slices of pillowy apple-studded bread that you can easily tear from the loaf.

Get the recipe: Cinnamon-Apple Pull-Apart Bread

To make this recipe, you'll need: SAF Instant Yeast
